hints.title: In-Place Matrix Rotation Obstacle
hints.text: Rotating an NxN matrix 90 degrees clockwise by creating an auxiliary 2D grid violates the O(1) extra space constraint. How can geometric symmetry (transposition and reflection) achieve the rotation in place?

hints.title: Transpose Then Reflect Invariant
hints.text: A 90-degree clockwise rotation is mathematically equivalent to transposing the matrix across its main diagonal, followed by reversing each row horizontally.

hints.title: Two-Step Transformation Procedure
hints.text: First, transpose the matrix: for every row i from 0 to n - 1 and column j from i + 1 to n - 1, swap matrix[i][j] with matrix[j][i]. Second, reverse each row: for each row i, reverse the elements in-place.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: dimension of square matrix (1 <= N <= 20)
complexity.notes: Every cell is swapped a constant number of times in O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Allocating a new result grid violates the in-place O(1) auxiliary memory requirement.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Zero auxiliary allocations by utilizing matrix transposition and reflection.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Knowing the mathematical equivalence of 90-degree rotation to transpose + reverse.
